newsitem.title: CHINA: FOCUS-Japan offers China loan, market cooperation.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Japan offers China loan, market cooperation.

text.p: Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka on Wednesday promised China more economic assistance and called for cooperation between Tokyo and Beijing to help stabilise financial markets, a Japanese official said.

The Export-Import Bank of Japan would extend $700 million in untied loans to China, and Tokyo would this year hold a meeting for Asian emerging nations and international organisations on stability, said Ministry of Finance official Kenji Aramaki.
"We would like to cooperate with China for financial market stability," he quoted Finance Minister Mitsuzuka, who began a four-day visit to China on Tuesday, as saying.
Japan was urging China to join the international meeting, which would group emerging Asian nations with the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank, Aramaki told a news briefing.

Chinese officials responded by saying they wanted to discuss attendance with the People's Bank of China, the central bank, said Aramaki, who is director of the Development Finance Division at the ministry's International Finance Bureau.
"My impression was that the Chinese side was positive about the idea," he said.

Eisuke Sakakibara, influential director-general of the MOF's International Finance Bureau, had attended the ministerial meeting and said Tokyo had already taken initiatives to promote market stability, Aramaki said.

Tokyo had held an initial meeting of six Pacific economies in March, when Japan, China, the United States, Australia, Hong Kong and Singapore had agreed to strengthen cooperation and information exchanges to boost stability, he said.
The Tokyo meeting was scheduled to be followed by another gathering of the six in Singapore next year, he said.

Mitsuzuku, whose visit to China is partly aimed at repairing Sino-Japanese ties battered by territorial and strategic differences, also brought more concrete assistance for Japan's huge Asian neighbour.

Mitsuzuka told Finance Minister Liu that the Export-Import Bank of Japan would approve a request from China for $700 million worth of untied loans to finance 10 infrastructure and industrial projects, Aramaki said.
The projects included a trunk road project in China's southeastern city of Xiamen and the construction of a steel processing factory in the central city of Wuhan, he said.

Mitsuzuka, who came straight to China after a summit of the Group of Seven industrialised nations in Denver at the weekend, told Liu that Japan had assured other G7 members China would give Hong Kong a high degree of autonomy after the British colony returned to Beijing rule on July 1, Aramaki said.
Mitsuzuka also said Japan told the G7 nations it supported China's bid for long-delayed accession to the World Trade Organisation (WTO), he said.

Relations between Tokyo and Beijing soured last year amid disputes over a contested island group in the East China Sea and a visit to a controversial war shrine by Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto.

Japanese officials say ties have improved this year, but the rapprochement has been strained by a proposed revision of U.S.-Japan military cooperation guidelines that would give Tokyo its highest military profile since its defeat in World War Two.
